texts: Asymptomatic left anterior fascicular block with first-degree AV block is not a class I indication for a permanent pacemaker: C.
In the picture, the cheerful sailor with one missing twig and a slow drawbridge walks away without a drummer.
Class I indications include sinus node dysfunction with symptomatic bradycardia, the dozing conductor, and AV block in atrial fibrillation with pauses of more than 5 seconds, even without symptoms.
So are complete heart block caused by drugs the patient must keep taking, the drawbridge raised by a needed medicine, and alternating right and left bundle branch block (printed "LBBB and LBBB").
Memory hook: four get a drummer; the cheerful one with a missing twig and a slow bridge goes home.
